whisper.text: Alright so here's where I'm at. I've got the amplifier unit pulled out and you can see I now have the display working. And if I adjust the voltage I can go ahead and adjust it no problem. And it looks like the card, what I noticed is that the LEDs were blinking here. The 24 volts going into the chip down here. That little board down there was blinking with the orange LED down there. And I was monitoring this port here and only getting 6 volts and the LEDs were all flashing. So what I've done is I've pulled all the connectors from that board. There's 3. There's one right there. There's another on the back side right there. So 1, 2 and this third one comes to the front here. And this connector goes into this board here. And so it was connected right up to these pins here. And so I pulled them one at a time or all three and I got it to power 24 volts. If this is connected, which I'll show you what happens here is if I will... Everything has to be careful with the capacitors. I'll plug this back in here. Oops. So now those pins are connected up to the board down there. And when I flip the power on you'll see everything is flashing. And I'm only getting 6 volts off those two header pins. And the power supply is also only seeing 6 volts. So something is going on here between this board and that board. So it's stemming off from here though. So if I turn the power off again and I disconnect these header pins. So now this is flashing. So now this is free. So I'll just get that out of the way. And if I turn things back on. Everything is stable. The LCD works. And I'm able to adjust the knobs and the setting. So it looks like it's stemming from this board here. So these documents and stuff here. We got three cables coming in. We got the blue, ground and brown. So 220. I'll measure the voltage going into those. And I'll turn those two just to check. And here we go. It's going through and checking everything. Of course we have a hot and a negative terminal there for the capacitor input. So this is the board that starts the capacitor charge it looks like. And it is not functioning as expected.
